source_evidence: Interval funds will only buy back a certain percent—5% to 25%—of all outstanding shares during a repurchase offer.
answer: An interval fund repurchase offer is a limited opportunity to sell shares back to the fund. Offers generally occur every three, six, or twelve months, and the fund sets a deadline to accept; the actual repurchase happens later. The fund may accept requests for only a portion of its outstanding shares. If requests exceed the amount available, repurchases are generally handled pro rata, so you may not be able to sell all the shares you requested. You cannot sell whenever you want, and shareholders who do not accept an offer generally must wait for the next one.
